how: Six weeks before the S&P 500. The Nasdaq fell 36.4% to 28 December 2022.
First session of the year. The index fell 25.4% over the next 195 sessions.

t: VIX closing high of the whole bear market: 36.5
how: S&P 500 −2.95% to 4201.09. The VIX never closed higher, including at the June and October lows.
Inside an 11.1% rally from 8 to 29 March, which failed.
Close 3749.63. VIX 34.0, below its March high.
The gain was reversed the next session with a fall of 3.3%.
34.8% of the study’s stocks at 52-week lows, the most of the bear market. A 17.4% rally began here.

t: Breadth thrust on the S&P 1500, eleven weeks early
how: Close 4072.43. The index made a new low in October but was higher a year later.

t: Summer rally stops one point under the 200-day average
how: Intraday high 4325.28 against an average of 4326.18. Close 4305.20, up 17.4% from June.
Close 4057.66. The rally was over; the June low broke a month later.

t: −4.3%: leveraged funds sell $15.5bn into the close
how: Nomura’s estimate of end-of-day selling. The index lost a further 8.8% over the next 13 sessions.
The June low had broken on 26 September. SPY volume was 1.9 times its average, the heaviest near the final low, eight sessions before it.
VIX 33.6; volume normal; 15.5% of stocks at 52-week lows against 34.8% in June.

t: Inflation above forecasts: new low, then +2.6%
how: Intraday low 3491.58, close 3669.91. The low of the bear market came on bad news.
Seventh session after the low. Three earlier ones in 2022 had failed by the research file’s count.
Close 3956.37, the largest gain of the year. Core inflation 6.3%.
Session 34, 14.1% above the low. Lost again three sessions later.
S&P 500 −0.6% to 3995.32. The index fell 5.3% over the next two weeks.
S&P 500 at 3783.22, 5.8% above its October low. Large growth stocks turned after this date.

t: NYSE breadth thrust, 63 sessions after the low
how: Advances 2.16 times declines over ten days by Deemer’s rule. Close 3983.17, 11.4% above the low.
